title: Pha That Luang
summary: Pha That Luang is a golden stupa about 45 m tall on a hill in Vientiane, Laos. King Setthathirath is credited with building it in 1566, the year he moved the capital from Luang Prabang, on the site of an older stupa believed to hold a relic of the Buddha. Invaders damaged it several times and it was restored each time; it appears on the national coat of arms.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 1566 construction date given by the NIU SEAsite page; the sacredsites.com page instead calls 1566 the start of the first documented restoration. End is the present.
